{{Short description|Type of Calculator}}
{{Orphan|date=June 2019}}

The '''QAMA Calculator''' is a [[calculator]] that requires users to provide a reasonable estimate of the answer before the precise answer is delivered.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://qamacalculator.com/|title=Introducing QAMA Calculator|website=qamacalculator.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/alexknapp/2012/07/09/qama-the-calculator-that-makes-you-better-at-math/#32d3b4a16a91|title=QAMA: The Calculator That Makes You Better At Math|first=Alex|last=Knapp|website=[[Forbes]] |publisher=}}</ref> QAMA stands for Quick Approximate Mental [[Arithmetic]].

Invented by Ilan Samson, it aims to get users to think first by estimating before they get the correct answer.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://ideas.time.com/2012/11/29/how-to-use-technology-to-make-you-smarter/?iid=op-main-lead|title=How to Use Technology to Make You Smarter|last=Paul|first=Annie Murphy|magazine=Time|access-date=2018-08-23|language=en-US|issn=0040-781X}}</ref> [[Estimation]] is seen by many as an essential part of [[mathematics]], and some believe that the presence and popularity of calculators could inhibit the use of estimation skills.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goodreads.com/quotes/846896-when-an-official-report-in-the-uk-was-commissioned-to|title=A quote from What's Math Got to Do with It?|website=www.goodreads.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://munews.missouri.edu/news-releases/2008/0528-reys-lifetime-award-release.php|title=Power of Estimation Takes Math Beyond Classroom - MU News Bureau|website=munews.missouri.edu|access-date=2018-08-20|archive-date=2018-08-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180824101753/https://munews.missouri.edu/news-releases/2008/0528-reys-lifetime-award-release.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>

A physical version of the calculator was released for sale in 2014, with [[Mobile app|apps]] for smartphones and tablets developed in 2016.
